subject: FastRetail checkout timeouts — timeout/retry amplification investigation
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Checkout failures — p95/p99 spikes during peak window

Diego —

We're seeing a surge of checkout failures this morning between 08:50–09:05 PDT. Our frontend reports ~1.8% of checkout attempts timing out (client-side) and a sharp jump in perceived p95/p99 latency. This correlates with a drop in completed orders. Attached is a small log excerpt from our side (fastretail-checkout-sample.log).

Can you confirm whether this is an upstream Redwood API regression? We weren't throttled on our end and haven't changed client timeouts in the last deploy. This is impacting several large merchants — we need guidance ASAP.

— Alex
Senior SRE, FastRetail
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures — p95/p99 spikes during peak window

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the log. I'm opening an incident with Eng and we'll prioritize this. Initial questions:

- Can you confirm the client SDK version and retry settings?
- Any signs of client-side retries (duplicate request IDs) in the log excerpt?
- Is the traffic spike limited to a segment of your users or global?

Putting Sean and Marissa on the thread to triage. Short term, if you can temporarily increase client timeout to 12s and disable auto-retries that would help isolate a server-side regression vs a client amplification loop. I'll follow up with an ETA for a deeper investigation.

— Diego
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: FastRetail checkout failures — immediate triage request

Forwarding FastRetail's sample and metrics. Impact: revenue drop and exec attention. Customer insists this started with no client-side changes. Please prioritize correlation between our p95/p99 and any burst of identical requests (potential retry amplification).

Attachments: fastretail-checkout-sample.log (from customer)

Thanks — Diego
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: FastRetail checkout failures — immediate triage request

Quick summary from logs we pulled (internal): we see a ~4.5x increase in identical request fingerprints during the window Alex reported. Our ingress shows retries clustered within <200ms of an initial request which amplifies backend load and temporarily increases queueing on the serving fleet; p95/p99 jump follows the retry bursts by ~30–60s.

Hypothesis: client-side SDK with aggressive retry/backoff parameters caused a retry storm that correlates with the observed p95/p99 regression. Not seeing evidence of a model or kernel regression yet.

Immediate mitigation options:
- Apply a short-lived token-bucket throttle for high-rate request fingerprints from that FastRetail API key (server-side, 5min)
- Return a 429 for churned fingerprints to force client backoff
- Recommend FastRetail disable SDK auto-retries and increase timeout as isolation step

Can infra run a quick dedupe process on the 09:00 window (grep request_id) and share counts? Also need a sampled set of full traces to confirm queueing contribution.

— Sean
Sr. Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FastRetail checkout failures — recommended next steps

Alex — thanks for sharing the log. From a customer-impact perspective: we'd like to give you two parallel paths — (1) immediate operational mitigations you can apply client-side, (2) short server-side protection while we validate root cause.

Client-side recommendations (temporary):
- disable SDK auto-retries (config flag: auto_retry: false)
- increase request timeout to 12s
- enable jittered exponential backoff for idempotent calls only

Server-side (Redwood) actions we will take now:
- enable a 5-minute fingerprint-based soft-throttle for your API key
- sample full traces from 08:45–09:10 and share via S3 link
- engage runtime team to watch kernel queues and mem utilization during the window

I'll share a short support runbook and a tiny patch you can drop into the SDK to disable retries; attaching sdk-retry-config-diff.patch and support-runbook-disable-auto-retry.md.

— Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: FastRetail — immediate mitigation applied and next steps

Alex — we applied the server-side soft-throttle for your API key and sampled full traces; infra confirmed a reduction in duplicate fingerprints and queue depth beginning 09:08. Please try the following on your side and reply with results:

1) flip auto_retry: false (we provided patch)
2) increase client timeout to 12s

We'll have a short incident wrap-up and propose a permanent change to SDK retry defaults if this confirms client amplification. Can we schedule a 30-minute executive briefing for Monday to review impact and credits? I can bring Eng and CS leads.

— Diego
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fastretail.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 16:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FastRetail — immediate mitigation applied and next steps

Diego/Marissa —

We applied the disable-auto-retry patch and bumped the timeout this morning. Early numbers show checkout errors down to 0.3% and p99 returning to baseline. Thank you for the quick response.

For the exec call: Monday at 11:00 PT works for us. We'd like a timeline for a permanent fix (SDK default change + server-side safeguards) and to discuss a good-will credit for the affected window.

— Alex
